run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T06:50:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is explained by a rollout restart of the single-replica Deployment otel-demo/ad at 2026-11-17T06:49:02Z. The old ad pod was killed at 06:49:04 and the replacement pod was reported Ready at 06:49:04 (the ad container defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe), yet the ad application only logged 'Ad service starting.' at 06:53:44 and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 06:55:24, serving its first request at 06:56:59. ad produced no AdService/GetAds spans from about 06:50:30 to 06:58:30 while every frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client span was an error, and frontend's error-span rate rose from a zero baseline to 8.04/s (peak at 06:52) and 4.422/s at 06:54, the exact value in the alert annotation, then fell to 0 by 07:00. The same restart pattern on Deployment otel-demo/payment (restarted 06:49:01) coincides with a short checkout sub-burst confined to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (06:51:30-06:53:00). Load was flat (about 60-70 frontend spans/s) and nodes had no pressure, so neither explains the burst. ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config still declares adFailure and paymentUnreachable as 'on'; this remains an unconfirmed hypothesis because ad and payment demonstrably served traffic successfully later in the burst (ad 06:57-06:58:49, payment 'Transaction complete' 06:57:58-06:58:42) and frontend/checkout error rates were 0 at 07:00-07:01 while those flags still read 'on'. Who triggered the 06:49 rollout restarts is unknown because change history is not integrated.

claims.text: frontend's error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was 0 from 06:29:05 through 06:49:05, was 0.478/s at the 06:50:05 sample, peaked at 8.044/s at 06:52, read 4.422222222222222 at 06:54 (the exact value in the alert annotation), fell to 1.251/s at 06:59:05 and was 0 at 07:00 and 07:01.

frontend's error spans concentrate on two chains: the home-page/ad chain, where span_name GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds all show the identical rate 1.1889/s at 06:52, and the checkout chain, where POST, POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder show 0.8/s at 06:52, plus tcp.connect at 0.0889/s. No frontend error rate appears for GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, CartService or ProductCatalogService spans.

frontend-proxy recorded the same burst on its own spans: span_name 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' error rates rose to 1.944/s at 06:52 and tapered to 0.0177/s at 07:01, mirroring frontend's errors at the edge.

The ad service stopped producing GetAds spans during the burst: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds rate was 1.5-1.93/s up to 06:50:00, 0 from 06:50:30 to 06:58:30, and 1.667/s at 07:00, while over the same period frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans were ERROR at 1.3-2.1/s and STATUS_CODE_UNSET was 0, so the calls did not reach ad.

Deployment otel-demo/ad was rollout-restarted at 06:49:02: its generation is 2 and the new ReplicaSet ad-5f8dd7c58d carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:49:02Z with an otherwise identical pod template (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, same env and container spec); ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 was scaled to 0 and pod ad-554b849958-6z62j received a Killing event at 06:49:04.

The replacement ad pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 was created 06:49:02 and reported Ready (pod condition Ready=True at 06:49:04, container ready=true, restartCount 0, running since 06:49:04), but its application logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 06:53:44.972 and 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 06:55:24.975, with the first ad request ('Targeted ad request received for [assembly]') at 06:56:59.898.

The ad and payment container specs define no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, and set tight resources: ad limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi (requests 10m / 225Mi) and payment limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi; both Deployments are single-replica RollingUpdate with maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%.

The new ad pod was CPU-throttled far more than its predecessor: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total rate for ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 rose to 9.1-19.7/s from 06:50 to 06:56 while container_cpu_usage_seconds_total was about 0.044-0.098 cores against a 0.05-core limit, versus about 0.3-2.7/s of throttling and 0.005-0.021 cores of usage for the previous pod ad-554b849958-6z62j; the new payment pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn peaked at 18.6/s versus about 0.5-3.6/s for payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp.

Deployment otel-demo/payment was rollout-restarted at 06:49:01 (generation 2, restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:49:01Z); old pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp was killed at 06:49:05 and new pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn was created 06:49:01, its container started 06:49:05 and the pod reported Ready at 06:49:05, while the application logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 06:50:26.46. payment's own error-span rate stayed 0 throughout the window.

checkout's error spans are exactly two span names, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (checkout's client call to payment), at 0.42-0.72/s from 06:51:30 to 06:53:00 and zero afterwards; no other checkout child call (cart, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog, fraud-detection) appears with errors.

Only three otel-demo Deployments carry a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation: ad (06:49:02Z), payment (06:49:01Z) and flagd (06:18:11Z); every other Deployment in the namespace, including frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, cart, product-catalog, currency, email, shipping, recommendation, accounting, quote, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, postgresql, valkey-cart and fraud-detection, is generation 1 with no restartedAt.
Load was not a factor: frontend's total span rate stayed at about 59-70 spans/s throughout 06:37-07:01, dipping to 37.2 at 06:51 and 30.6 at 06:59, with no surge around the 06:49-06:50 error onset.
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and NetworkUnavailable=False at query time, so node-level resource pressure is not the explanation.

Service and Endpoint configuration for the implicated services is consistent at query time: Service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad and targets port 8080, Service payment selects opentelemetry.io/name=payment, and Endpoints ad (100.96.1.149:8080 named tcp-service) and payment (100.96.1.157:8080 named tcp-service) each have one address, so no selector or port mismatch is visible.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config was created 2026-11-17T06:16:14Z (helm-managed) and its data key 'demo.flagd.json' declares adFailure defaultVariant "on" (description 'Fail ad service') and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant "on" (description 'Payment service is unavailable'), both with state ENABLED, while every other flag is off; Deployment flagd mounts that ConfigMap as volume config-ro into a writable emptyDir config-rw read by the flagd container at /etc/flagd.

ad and payment themselves processed traffic successfully later in the burst: the ad pod logged repeated 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received' lines from 06:57:00 to 06:58:49, and the payment pod logged 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs from 06:57:58.66 through 06:58:42.99.

fraud-detection's container terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 06:50:48, restarted at 06:50:49 (restartCount 1) and its pod reported Ready at 06:50:50; Deployment fraud-detection has no probes and limits cpu 100m / memory 400Mi.

Root cause of the alert: Deployment otel-demo/ad was restarted at 06:49:02 and, because its pod template has no readiness probe, its replacement pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 was marked Ready at 06:49:04 while the ad application did not listen until 06:55:24; ad produced no GetAds spans from about 06:50:30 to 06:58:30 and frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans failed at 1.3-2.1/s over the same period, which is the dominant component of the frontend error-span rate that fired this alert.

The flagd fault flags do not match the observed behaviour well enough to be called the cause: the flagd-config ConfigMap already existed from 06:16:14 with adFailure and paymentUnreachable 'on', yet ad served GetAds successfully (UNSET, no error rate) right up to 06:50; ad logged successful ad requests 06:57:00-06:58:49 and payment logged 'Transaction complete.' 06:57:58-06:58:42 while both flags still read 'on'; and frontend and checkout error rates are 0 at 07:00-07:01 although the ConfigMap still declares those faults 'on'.

fraud-detection's OOMKill at 06:50:48 did not cause this alert: checkout's error spans during the burst are exclusively oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with no errored fraud-detection call, and the fraud-detection container restarted within one second with its pod Ready again at 06:50:50.

The roughly 4.7-minute gap between the ad container start (06:49:04) and its first log line 'Ad service starting.' (06:53:44) is consistent with CPU starvation: the new ad pod's usage of about 0.09 cores exceeded its 50m CPU limit and it was throttled at 9-20 periods/s, versus 0.3-2.7/s throttling and about 0.01 cores of usage for the pod it replaced. Causality between throttling and the startup delay is not directly proven.

The brief checkout sub-burst (PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge errors 06:51:30-06:53:00) is plausibly a consequence of Deployment otel-demo/payment's rollout restart at 06:49:01, where the replacement pod was Ready at 06:49:05 but its gRPC server only logged listening at 06:50:26 and payment's own spans show zero errors, i.e. checkout's Charge calls failed at the connection level; the 1-2 minute lag after payment started listening would then be gRPC client reconnection or backoff.

The two enabled fault-injection settings in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, adFailure ('Fail ad service') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), name exactly the two failing call paths seen here, so an injected-flag change around 06:49 remains a candidate cause; the countervailing evidence (successful ad and payment traffic later in the burst, zero error rates at 07:00-07:01 while both flags read 'on', and successful ad serving 06:42-06:50 with the same ConfigMap in place) means the flag values cannot be confirmed as active during the burst from the visible data.

Add a readinessProbe and startupProbe on the ad and payment containers so a pod is not added to Service endpoints before the application is listening, and raise their CPU limits (currently 50m for ad and 20m for payment) so application initialisation is not throttled; consider more than one replica and maxUnavailable 0 for these single-replica services so a rollout never removes the only serving pod.

Retrieve change and audit history to identify who issued the rollout restarts recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:49:02Z on Deployment ad and 2026-11-17T06:49:01Z on Deployment payment, and check the flagd runtime flag state (the writable /etc/flagd copy, which can diverge from ConfigMap flagd-config) for the same timestamp.

gaps: Change history is not integrated, so what or who triggered the rollout restarts of Deployment ad (06:49:02Z) and Deployment payment (06:49:01Z) is unknown; no audit trail is available.

Jaeger's most recent traces end at 2026-11-17T06:33:38 (the traces_search view 6bd01a08-cbc4-4ee3-b975-addd2acb3bf3-t0:fe1c870a-6937-4a54-901a-dd4d2e8d8204 was also too large to return), before the error burst, so no trace-level error details (gRPC status codes, error messages, parent-child linkage) exist for the failing frontend, checkout or ad spans; tag and time-bounded trace searches d37b9149-8c30-4ec6-af26-2abd1c1746b6-t0:63c62063-ab13-43a2-bdb1-0d38eccbd014 and 644be951-e538-434e-8348-b3908f1735d9-t1:fd3bb409-e615-4bc9-b30b-ec01218a5a53 returned no_data.

The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr log lines in the 06:45-07:05 window (queries 084ca032-6e82-4f80-a5b5-2129be6d0468-t0:a403038f-962a-4552-96cb-7fe6dd595fda and 6bd01a08-cbc4-4ee3-b975-addd2acb3bf3-t2:94af6869-fa3f-4fa4-98e8-b7a8b0bd66d9 returned no_data), so no frontend application error text is available to explain the failures.

gRPC status codes for the failed calls are unknown: rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count label lookups (7698e522-3a54-4835-9e12-53ae31f4b71f-t0:d3769a71-73f3-415c-a712-f340d5dfb23a and 7698e522-3a54-4835-9e12-53ae31f4b71f-t1:2f2caa51-ac54-41a3-8899-0b541aeb1040), the http_server_request_duration_seconds_count label lookup (4b7eaeb8-5cdf-4c75-933d-ba6805a56772-t1:66334a30-956f-434b-93f0-f54ad0dc7214), the rpc_client_duration query (6416f712-ae1c-4ad1-a75d-ba028a219c06-t0:9aa7eb86-663b-4935-ad32-fa6b0696e114) and app_payment_transactions_total (6cd546c2-6f3b-421b-99bb-7d18574b727b-t1:9b566055-67b0-4803-b943-903dfe7fb7f8) all returned no_data, leaving ERROR/UNSET span status as the only status information.

Whether the flagd runtime flag state (the emptyDir /etc/flagd copy used by flagd and editable by the flagd-ui container) had adFailure or paymentUnreachable enabled during 06:49-07:00 could not be verified; only the seed ConfigMap flagd-config is readable, and it reads 'on' now and as far back as its 06:16:14Z creation timestamp.

The reason the ad container took about 4.7 minutes from container start (06:49:04) to its first log line (06:53:44) is not directly evidenced; heavy CPU throttling against the 50m limit was observed but not proven to be the cause.

The ad pod's logs end at 06:58:49 (and later ad log reads returned no_data: cfb7079a-3e4e-4f82-981b-1c5238f8c805-t1:12f84c40-92e2-4f47-a0d8-50f38695fdd6) and frontend's error metric data ends at 07:01:00, so ad's serving state and frontend's error rate after those times are unknown.

Kubernetes metric lookups for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_* series returned no_data (4b7eaeb8-5cdf-4c75-933d-ba6805a56772-t0:6aea3024-a67b-4625-8778-822292c24a3f, cfb7079a-3e4e-4f82-981b-1c5238f8c805-t0:b273fdef-5186-4aca-8f66-29a7216b02bc), so workload readiness is evidenced only by pod conditions and events, not by a kube-state-metrics series.

Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in namespace otel-demo returned no objects (107b4aee-7921-417a-a33d-5aa38c89ff5b-t2:19150a23-01a7-45d0-b9c3-d244df4b6bc4 and 107b4aee-7921-417a-a33d-5aa38c89ff5b-t3:09daf9e7-fe98-43e5-9f80-69f17f4412b0, both no_data); those empty results are not evidence that no such objects exist.

Prometheus alert-rule lookups for RequestErrorRate (084ca032-6e82-4f80-a5b5-2129be6d0468-t1:6f1e143d-820f-45b7-8d1f-af4c42c2c491 and 6bd01a08-cbc4-4ee3-b975-addd2acb3bf3-t3:38a82188-70a7-401c-bdac-e6f674f32288) returned no_data, so the alert's exact PromQL expression and evaluation window could not be read.
next_steps: Review Kubernetes audit/change history for the kubectl rollout restart actions on Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 2026-11-17T06:49:01-02Z and for any edit to ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config or to flagd runtime flags in that window.
Inspect the live flagd configuration (its /etc/flagd copy or UI state) to confirm whether adFailure and paymentUnreachable were enabled during 06:49-07:00, rather than relying on the seed ConfigMap.
Add readiness/startup probes and increase CPU limits for ad and payment, and run at least two replicas with maxUnavailable 0, then verify a rollout no longer removes the only serving instance.
If trace-level detail is needed, capture a fresh reproduction while Jaeger is retaining recent traces, and check the frontend's gRPC status codes for AdService/GetAds during the outage.

ad and payment themselves processed traffic successfully later in the burst: the ad pod logged repeated 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received' lines from 06:57:00 to 06:58:49, and the payment pod logged 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs from 06:57:58.66 through 06:58:42.99.

fraud-detection's container terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 06:50:48, restarted at 06:50:49 (restartCount 1) and its pod reported Ready at 06:50:50; Deployment fraud-detection has no probes and limits cpu 100m / memory 400Mi.

Root cause of the alert: Deployment otel-demo/ad was restarted at 06:49:02 and, because its pod template has no readiness probe, its replacement pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 was marked Ready at 06:49:04 while the ad application did not listen until 06:55:24; ad produced no GetAds spans from about 06:50:30 to 06:58:30 and frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans failed at 1.3-2.1/s over the same period, which is the dominant component of the frontend error-span rate that fired this alert.

hypothesis.text: The roughly 4.7-minute gap between the ad container start (06:49:04) and its first log line 'Ad service starting.' (06:53:44) is consistent with CPU starvation: the new ad pod's usage of about 0.09 cores exceeded its 50m CPU limit and it was throttled at 9-20 periods/s, versus 0.3-2.7/s throttling and about 0.01 cores of usage for the pod it replaced. Causality between throttling and the startup delay is not directly proven.

The brief checkout sub-burst (PlaceOrder and PaymentService/Charge errors 06:51:30-06:53:00) is plausibly a consequence of Deployment otel-demo/payment's rollout restart at 06:49:01, where the replacement pod was Ready at 06:49:05 but its gRPC server only logged listening at 06:50:26 and payment's own spans show zero errors, i.e. checkout's Charge calls failed at the connection level; the 1-2 minute lag after payment started listening would then be gRPC client reconnection or backoff.

The two enabled fault-injection settings in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, adFailure ('Fail ad service') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), name exactly the two failing call paths seen here, so an injected-flag change around 06:49 remains a candidate cause; the countervailing evidence (successful ad and payment traffic later in the burst, zero error rates at 07:00-07:01 while both flags read 'on', and successful ad serving 06:42-06:50 with the same ConfigMap in place) means the flag values cannot be confirmed as active during the burst from the visible data.

recommendation.text: Add a readinessProbe and startupProbe on the ad and payment containers so a pod is not added to Service endpoints before the application is listening, and raise their CPU limits (currently 50m for ad and 20m for payment) so application initialisation is not throttled; consider more than one replica and maxUnavailable 0 for these single-replica services so a rollout never removes the only serving pod.

Retrieve change and audit history to identify who issued the rollout restarts recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T06:49:02Z on Deployment ad and 2026-11-17T06:49:01Z on Deployment payment, and check the flagd runtime flag state (the writable /etc/flagd copy, which can diverge from ConfigMap flagd-config) for the same timestamp.

counter_evidence.text: The flagd fault flags do not match the observed behaviour well enough to be called the cause: the flagd-config ConfigMap already existed from 06:16:14 with adFailure and paymentUnreachable 'on', yet ad served GetAds successfully (UNSET, no error rate) right up to 06:50; ad logged successful ad requests 06:57:00-06:58:49 and payment logged 'Transaction complete.' 06:57:58-06:58:42 while both flags still read 'on'; and frontend and checkout error rates are 0 at 07:00-07:01 although the ConfigMap still declares those faults 'on'.

rejected_hypothesis.text: fraud-detection's OOMKill at 06:50:48 did not cause this alert: checkout's error spans during the burst are exclusively oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with no errored fraud-detection call, and the fraud-detection container restarted within one second with its pod Ready again at 06:50:50.
